subject: Next steps: AlphaSys trial traffic ingestion & acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@alphasys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps: AlphaSys trial traffic ingestion & acceptance criteria

Thanks again for the call earlier, Jordan — great to meet the AlphaSys team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth heading into the POC: 

1) Trial objective and acceptance criteria
- Primary objective: validate Redwood inference can serve AlphaSys's realtime recommendation API at target latency and cost.
- Acceptance (pass/fail): p95 generation latency <= 220ms for the 99% of production-like requests; sustained throughput >= 120 RPS with <1% error rate; peak bursts up to 600 RPS handled without manual intervention.

2) Measurement plan
- Metrics we'll track in the console: p50/p95/p99 latency, request success rate, tokens generated, cost per 1M tokens.
- We'll capture a 72-hour ramp (steady-state + burst windows) and provide CSV traffic exports for your team.

3) Workload/traffic profile we need from AlphaSys (see section below) — if you can attach a sample CSV it helps accelerate set up:
- Average steady RPS target: please provide minutes-level histogram if available.
- Typical prompt length (input tokens) and expected average output tokens.
- Peak concurrency (simultaneous open requests / KV cache sizes).
- Burst pattern: frequency/duration of spikes (examples: daily 09:00-09:15, weekly Monday 00:00).

4) Timeline & owners
- Proposed kickoff (environment ready): Jan 18 start of smoke tests.
- 1 week smoke + 2 week evaluation. Final signoff by Feb 8.
- Redwood owners: Lauren (trial PM), Marissa (commercial lead), Dev Patel (ingest/ops lead).
- AlphaSys owners: Jordan and Priya (cc).

5) Next actions (please):
- Jordan: share a representative traffic CSV and any auth requirements for test tokens by Jan 14.
- AlphaSys: confirm preferred model family (open model / quantized variant) and whether payloads include tool calls/structured output.
- Redwood: will provision a dedicated trial slot, send initial runbook and shared Drive link.

Attachments: I attached a blank CSV template and a one-page POC success criteria doc for quick edits.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
[Attachment: POC-success-criteria-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@alphasys.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@alphasys.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 17:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: AlphaSys trial traffic ingestion & acceptance criteria

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline plus the sample traffic attached.

- Steady-state: 120 RPS average across our US region (5-minute rolling average). We have a 3x difference between low and high hours.
- Burst behavior: primary bursts are morning commerce events — we see spikes to ~600 RPS lasting 6-18 minutes, 3x per day during promos.
- Tokens: input prompts ~40-80 tokens; typical generated outputs ~120 tokens; 95th percentile outputs up to 420 tokens.
- Concurrency: concurrent open requests typically 200-250; during bursts we get to ~800 concurrent sockets.
- Model: plan to use an open Llamax-derived generation model (we'd like to test 8-bit quantized variant if supported).

Success criteria from our side: p95 <= 200ms for single-turn recs under steady-state; <2% downstream latency degradation for our front-end; no unhandled errors during a 600 RPS burst. If you can report expected cost estimates for the two-week trial that helps our procurement.

Attached: alphasy s-traffic-sample.csv (sanitized), includes per-request token counts and timestamps.

We can confirm providing test API keys scoped to trial environment. Target start date Jan 18 works.

—Jordan
Jordan Lee
Lead Platform Engineer, AlphaSys
jordan.lee@alphasys.com
[Attachment: alphasys-traffic-sample.csv (text/csv)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@alphasys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: AlphaSys trial traffic ingestion & acceptance criteria

Great — thanks for the sample, Jordan, that helps a lot. TL;DR: we can support the requested profile but want to confirm a few operational clarifications and commit owners/measurements for the run.

Planned Redwood trial plan (brief):
- Jan 18–19: provision dedicated trial slot + run short smoke tests with synthetic traffic.
- Jan 20–24: replay AlphaSys sample traffic in staging to validate batching and KV cache behavior.
- Jan 25–Feb 5: live trial window with monitoring and two planned burst injection windows (we'll coordinate exact times).

Acceptance checklist (concrete items we will sign off on):
- Measured p95 <= 220ms for the canonical request sample set during steady-state.
- Error rate <1% for 72h steady window and <2% during burst injections.
- No more than 15% request degradation to your front-end observed; we will correlate traces.
- Hand-off doc with recommended batching and quantization profile for production run.

Owners: Marissa will share a short commercial note (trial duration, any trial discounts) and Dev will confirm ingestion endpoints and tokens. Dev — can you confirm we can accept the CSV format Jordan sent and whether we need per-request session ids to emulate KV cache behavior?

Related links: HubSpot deal RF-2026-0192 and I shared a read-only Drive folder with the POC map: https://drive.google.com/file/d/alpha-poc-map

Lauren

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@alphasys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: AlphaSys trial traffic ingestion & acceptance criteria

Hi all — quick technical clarifications from the ingest/ops side before we kick off: 

1) CSV fields — the sample looks fine but we need a per-request session_id (to simulate KV cache warmup) and an iso8601 timestamp. If you can't provide session_id, we can synthesize using user_id bucket heuristics but results will differ.
2) Tokenization — which tokenizer variant did you use to compute token counts? We need to match tokenization for accurate cost/length estimates (Llamax vs standard Llama).
3) Model variant — confirm the exact package name & quantization (8-bit/4-bit). For heavy bursts we may switch to a variant with smaller memory footprint.
4) Auth & endpoint — send test API tokens to dev.ingest@redwood.com and indicate whether IP allow-listing is required.

If we have the above by Jan 15, we can fully provision the trial slot on Jan 17 for smoke tests on the 18th.

Thanks — Dev
Dev Patel
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: runbook-ingest-template.md (text/markdown) referenced]

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@alphasys.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@alphasys.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: AlphaSys trial traffic ingestion & acceptance criteria

Thanks Dev — we've added session_id and tokenizer column to the CSV and uploaded an updated file. Test tokens will be sent to dev.ingest@redwood.com and we will not IP-restrict for the trial window.

We confirm Jan 18 smoke test schedule and ready to proceed with the live window starting Jan 25. One note from procurement: we need a short estimate for expected trial spend (rough $) to our finance lead before generating a temporary PO; Marissa, can you share that?

Attaching updated sample.

—Jordan
